head: 9cfa05635897b7d37d08a6af5ffa17cec9b25dda
summary:
Fail. The issue outcome is still not delivered.

What this head fixes: reconcile() now calls block_unadmitted before settle for admitted PRs with the safe holds review_missing, review_target_record_unknown and latest_review_not_success. A never-reviewed PR therefore no longer keeps its guard, and a test that runs two wakes in a row covers this. Recovery before the first status works when no merge request exists (cancel_blocked → block_unadmitted → settle).

What is still missing:
- recovery_entry.verify_rollout always refuses. Every guarded writer, adoption publisher and recovery wake stops before any issue write, so after a real asynchronous native merge the linked issue stays open (as in Core #75, #77 and #79).
- There is no hosted asynchronous merge that closes its issue.
- There is no controlled hosted test of the issues:write permission hypothesis.
- Actor and launcher adoption are unproven.
- Request ownership is unproven, and safe cancellation is not implemented.
- A queued request whose guard is held by another run can stay blocked, and that guard retained, forever.

New liveness defect: the release path covers only the three safe-hold reasons. An admitted PR held for any other reason keeps its guard forever: CI pending or failing, qualification_not_ready, a changed issue, or verification_or_provider_failed. Later wakes cannot acquire the guard, so they skip that PR (guard_unavailable). If CI fails and the issue returns to todo, no worker can reclaim it. Only the disabled recovery workflow could release such a guard.

Existing CI, performance, review, protected-branch, no-bypass and failure-to-todo gates are preserved. No schedule is deployed, and other sessions' worktrees and leases are preserved.

findings.title: Verified post-merge closure remains unreachable
findings.detail: verify_rollout unconditionally raises recovery_rollout_not_verified. Every guarded writer, adoption publisher and recovery entry calls it before any write. No recovery workflow is deployed. After an asynchronous native merge, the linked issue therefore stays open.
findings.required_fix: Implement and review a rollout-evidence verifier. Deploy the recovery workflow through reviewed policy adoption. Then demonstrate automatic closure.

findings.title: No hosted asynchronous merge with automatic close proof
findings.detail: All controls are synthetic. The only real-provider fixture (Core #77) records a manual close.
findings.required_fix: Run a controlled hosted asynchronous native merge in which the mechanism closes the linked issue, together with hosted negative controls.

findings.title: issues:write permission hypothesis not tested
findings.detail: The issue requires a controlled hosted comparison before any production permission change or reliance on native auto-close. None is implemented or recorded.
findings.required_fix: Perform and document the controlled hosted permission comparison, keeping the exact CI, independent review and ownership gates.

findings.title: Guard retained forever for admitted PRs held for any non-safe reason
findings.detail: In reconcile, only the reasons review_missing, review_target_record_unknown and latest_review_not_success lead to block_unadmitted plus settle. Any other hold skips settle and keeps the merge guard: required_gates_not_success, qualification_not_ready, issue_not_eligible, verification_or_provider_failed and similar. On later wakes guarded.begin fails because the earlier completed run owns the guard, so the PR is only blocked (guard_unavailable) and is never re-evaluated. When the CI handoff returns the issue to todo, workers cannot claim it either. Only the disabled admission_recovery path could release such a guard.
findings.required_fix: For every refused or held admitted row with no merge request, establish and read back a blocking status, then settle (release) the guard. Add controls for CI-failed and qualification-held PRs across consecutive wakes.

findings.title: Queued-request guards and blocked queued PRs have no liveness path
findings.detail: cancel_blocked returns 'retained' when the PR is MERGED or a request exists, so a writer that died after queueing without a record keeps its guard forever. A later wake that fails guarded.begin calls block_unadmitted, which posts pending over the queued PR's success status. Nothing can restore approval.
findings.required_fix: Bind native request provenance to the guard so a later actor can safely take over, re-verify, republish success or cancel. Add recovery for a merge with no record, and controls for a queued PR followed by a later wake.

findings.title: Actor and launcher adoption and request ownership unproven
findings.detail: actor_rollout is always 'unknown'. request_history does not prove which run created a request. Cancellation and its race with merging are not implemented. The guard protocol requires every actor to adopt it.
findings.required_fix: Provide verified actor and launcher adoption evidence bound to the exact policy and runtime. Implement request-ownership provenance and safe cancellation.
